title: Knowledge check: Contributing to the Vue Ecosystem

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Contributing to the Vue Ecosystem”?
options: Upgrade every dependency at once without recording current behavior.
Assume Vue 2 automatically receives Vue 3 APIs.
Skip reproduction steps and deployment notes.
Inventory dependencies and existing behavior, add regression checks, change incrementally, and keep a rollback/documentation path.
questions.answer_key: Inventory dependencies and existing behavior, add regression checks, change incrementally, and keep a rollback/documentation path.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Contributing to the Vue Ecosystem directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Reading official documentation effectively”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Leave stale asynchronous work running and let it overwrite newer results.
Expect watch() to run immediately by default for every source.
Use watch() for explicit sources or watchEffect() for automatically tracked dependencies when a side effect is required; clean up asynchronous work.
Use computed() for every side effect.
questions.answer_key: Use watch() for explicit sources or watchEffect() for automatically tracked dependencies when a side effect is required; clean up asynchronous work.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Reading official documentation effectively”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Contributing to the Vue Ecosystem” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
